notes: Memsic 2125 is a 6-pin DIP straddling the breadboard centre gap in columns 17-19. Top row (left to right): GND, Y out, Temp. Bottom row: GND, X out, +5V (VDD). Pin mapping follows the schematic and the real chip pinout; the triangle marks the Temp/Y out/GND side.

Breadboard image is drawn with rows j-f in the top half; the catalogue names the top half bank 't' (rows a-e) and the bottom half 'b' (rows f-j). I used catalogue naming, so the sensor sits in 17-19t.e and 17-19b.f.
Exact rail hole numbers (bn.6, bn.12, bn.16) are approximate; each rail is one strip, so they all share the ground node.
Temp (TOUT) is not wired to anything.
Uno digital pin 2 goes to X out and pin 3 to Y out. Uno 5V goes to the sensor VDD, and Uno GND.1 goes through the bottom negative rail to both sensor GND pins.
The Arduino must be connected to the computer by USB for serial output, but no USB cable is shown in the circuit image, so none is added.
Tool note: the claude.ai Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive MCP servers need authorization via claude.ai connector settings. They are unavailable until then, and this task did not need them.
